editorText:
“Wait Shai! There’s another incoming. Short-range Missile detected, it appears to have broken off from the LRM and is closing on your position fast.”

Shai, stopped for a moment, her eyes focused steady with determination on the hanging pod afar hanging over the depths of the mountain saddle, then calm. “Only when you the trust the mother of the ocean, then you will dive the furthest reaches of her depths.” Her suit’s thrusters spun up a dark blue. Shai closed her eyes in silence for only a brief few seconds that felt like a rolling wave passing by in her mind. Then she opened her eyes and sprinted forward, jumping kneeling into the explosion as her legs discharged tstored energy into the grates below her they shuddered with a loud metallic clang, shifting from the immense force and the sudden displacement of weight as her thrusters burned with rich intense dark purple plumes like tiny space tulips accelerating her faster forward. The plumes stopped momentarily before she reached the ledge, then in unison they all erupted from the back of her suit, lifting her up, assisting her jump. She began picking up velocity, falling down as quickly as she had gone up. Then only after a second, she felt herself decelerating faster. Her suit’s thrusters had been blown out by a charged EMP explosion.

Tex and John sped to the edge of the grate, looking down into the valley below. All time slowed. Shai closed her eyes once more. “John, I’m activating manual override and reboot of my suit's systems.” “Do what you need to Shai, I’ll see you shortly,” “Captain” Shai shouted out excitedly, “I’ve, I’ve.” Tau was fixated on her wrist HUD, tapping away at this point.

Before John could even speak in response to her distress, Tex noticed a glowing purple light fastly approaching the edge of the underbelly on the 2nd Pod. “She’s done it,” Tex said with disbelief looking on in awe while grabbing out his stowed Railstorm on the lower rear of his suit.

John smiled, thinking to himself, “I knew she was a good pilot, she just needed a push.” Shai erupted from the fog, blasting out the cold icy weather from the pod's roof. Ice melted away beneath her, falling only to turn to icicles descending into the void. The slow burn of her suit's thrusters hummed an echo that spat back at her team, almost as if to be inviting them in. Arms of velvet hydrogen glowed, reaching around her giving an almost angelic appearance of wings as she slowly descended.  Her suit’s thrusters powered down with almost  synchronous timing as the contact magnetism in her boots peaked her suit's computer engaged their locking mechanism.  Her mag boots coils let out a crisp electronic hum, latching her to the solid steel roof of the pod. “That was some hot shit girly” Said Tex, looking over at Shai than down to the depths below, swallowing what smart remarks he had left in hesitation.

Shai re-engaged her suits thrusters blowing away what remained of the ice creating an even bigger landing area for the others still stranded across the valley. “The payload of the LRM SRM bank is small, only one,” Tao said as the others locked back their suits. One by one they all followed. Tao was next to make the leap, Tex behind her then John. In almost unison as though he was there to help her subtly. Then John was the last.

Proximity sensor on the Engine signature was getting stronger, Tau looked over concerned, her eyes fixed on John. John pressed jumped “Tao do you have anything? Kitten?”, John was hesitant but still cool. Then he went, charging like a bull and launching himself agile through the air, turning to the side when he did this. He turned using the assist of his suit thrusters to send him into a sideways barrel roll spinning in the air, dodging a barrage of missile small fires. The LRM sheer size had made it suitable for small to mid-calibre arms, enough to rattle a Protectant's armour.

He opened out his arms pointing directly at the LRM, tracking it quietly with patience. It was silent, and then it wasn’t anymore. John felt his mind ripped from his own shell. Kitten tapped into john’s vision feed. The long range missile went from a mere thermal blip to a clear burning contraption of death displayed across the others visors. After the object tracking software computed it’s trajectory heading straight for them, Kitten felt it apparent to warn them of what was coming their way. But John was all but silent, absent minded it seemed. Carefree.

Tor’s monitor flickered with static. A vague distant thermal imaging outline of figures resembling that of a protectant squad vanished from the screen then in a split second connection had all but been lost.

“We’ve lost control of the LRM!” said Tor, “What! how is that possible!” Marcellus lurched over Tor’s terminal, sneering in disbelief. “Get that missile back up or you’ll be promoted to Janitor!” Marcellus was red in the face. “But Athos! wasn’t that!” Athos cut Tor off, “I won’t repeat myself”.

The lost Facility

—————————————————

“I had some upgrades too Cap! when you got plugged into that we got plugged in, your neural code has been assimilated with mine” Kitten seemed ecstatic like she had found a new friend, then

John went silent and stopped firing. He could see himself outside of his body looking down straight on top of his team. He was not himself, but piloting a payload of death and destruction as the missiles targeting reticle converged on his point. He had control of the missile. A pristine three dimensional schematic illuminated the internal workings of the carrier of death. He thought hard, envisioning the missiles motors that steered it’s control surfaces. Motor actuators spun up as he flew through the circuits. slowly he began veering the missile off his direct course, steering it sharply back to where they had all just jumped from. He saw himself standing there like a statue drifting from vision as the targeting reticle lost vision of him. approaching an ever enlarging cavernous mouth.

John once certain he and the others were clear of the missiles strike zone, felt himself drawn back to his body, his vision coming back almost instantly. “I’ve got control again!” John croaked.

Sending it straight through the roof of the previous pod he had just jumped over. The explosion detonated almost a split second after it clonked through the steel roof, sending a wave shock that shook dagger like icicles from the overhead ridges. A barrage of teeth fell for John’s team only to break and shatter into oblivion on their armoured shoulders. The explosion was so powerful it sent the top of the cliff face they had just leaped from into an avalanche, enraged the mountain snow rock and rubble entombed the steel mountain halls of the lost facility from where they had just came. Leaving it hidden once again, silent, waiting to found again bearing history’s truth of the workerbot program for those who sought it.

The sound of screeching steel echoed the ravines that wound on for miles in either direction. Eventually the sound of metal and rock clashing sent shivers down his spine. The wire ropes sung and whipped under tension at the beckon of the wind. The grate bridges had lost some of their supporting wires in the explosion of the now relinquished missile. They croaked and moaned, hanging drunkenly in unforgiving icy winds. Snow ice and wind pelted against the pod’s shell slowly a heavy section  of ice that had accumulated atop the pod's dangling body began to slip. It was silent, and then once more it wasn’t. The loud crack of snapping steel wire ricochet off the mountain’s side. A mass of ice breaking into oblivion fell rapidly to the misty depths below.

The tattered pod shuddered, collapsing inward before expanding again, sending tremors through the entire structure. Loose wires began to fall, tugging at the ones still connected to John and his team, pulling them ever so slightly downward. The cables groaned under the strain, slowly dragging them deeper. The pod’s weight strained the wires to their breaking point, their groans swallowed by the biting wind. High-pressure oscillations vibrated through the lines, making the team's hairs stand on end as they listened to the ominous creaking. The pod, struck by the missile, now dangled precariously, its dozen supporting cables reduced to a fragile few. What remained was a desperate struggle for survival—both the pod and the lives of John, Tex, Tau, and Shai, clinging to the last threads of hope.

The hanging hidden facilities mountain interlink, like a lined up stack of dominoes, began breaking away from the Himalayan cliff face, falling like a snake out of a tree into the ravenous unknown below, bellowing out a symphony of snapping wires in the valley as it danced in the wind to its death below. Shai watched on. She felt the stomach’s of her teammates sink. Her and John’s team were about to go with it. Another supporting wire snapped.

John felt himself go cold again. He was flying through the pod's wiring infrastructure and electronic circuitry once more. He scaled the walls, he was right at the panel before he knew he had disconnected. The locking mechanism which resembled that of a 20th century train interlock, disengaged. The hanging station pod let go, Screeching steel could be heard as the final connecting face of the Pod link up cracked. strike zones. Licking the edges of the final connecting Pod, the pod John Tau and all his team now stood on lifted back calmly to it’s previous guys positions. They had all felt a touch of their new suits capabilities. They’d done it, and they’d done it elegantly. They looked at each other and then  to their now escape and shelter. John thought to himself

“I’m liking these new upgrades” John said walking towards another opening in the cliff face along what remained of the facility mountain pass. “We best take shelter” Steam bellowed from his helmet as he spoke the command softly.  Sherpa Rifles at the ready the others fell in line behind him.

“We need to recuperate our suit’s hydrogen reserves” Shai’s voice seemed chilled as she moved, listening carefully ahead at an almost uniform speed set by John. John was already at a large opening, except there were no blast doors or fortified facilities, only the shelter provided by re-enforced tunnels and cave. The winding tunnels had strata bolts drilled deep into the mountain to hold mesh of rock from crushing them. “I think we will be ok here for the time being” Said John. He looked around scanning the cave with his rifle. Something crunched beneath the weight of his suit. A used fireplace sat. “Only a couple weeks old” Tex walked over to the fireplace his shoulders relaxed his rifle at ease cradled in his forearm. He looked over at John. “Probably mountain locals prying, snooping about, they usually come up here to salvage parts”. Small jets of steam bellowed out of the chest on John’s Mark IV suit, John emerged from its splayed out chest cavity still slightly disorienting to the others as they looked on at what felt like his frail yet armoured body. As he stepped as soon as his hand lost touch with the suit’s shell it immediately closed back up turning about face and began guarding the entrance to the cave.

Tex had already begun harvesting ice off the cave face, still in his suit a strange tongue like contraption hugged the face of the cave creating a cupping bowl seal against the caves icy wall. As a his gauntlets ice burner melted columns of icicles along the wall water trickled into the strange contraption. Plumes of mist emitted from his shoulders out ports as the suit’s internal Electrolysis chamber separated hydrogen from the steady water stream. “You two get some rest, Me and Shai will keep watch” Tex didn’t look away while he talked, fixated,  just kept succing ice from the walls of the cavern. he made his way a fan like motion as a nano engineered suction cup moulded to the face, licking the walls like the tongue of a giant anteater. Tao climbed down from her suit, for it only to turn towards the descending tunnel in the other direction from where they had just entered. It walked seamlessly like a human, over to the steep downward tunnel that seemed to wind on forever into pitch blackness. A looming mist filled the belly of it, concealing it’s depths and what lay below from the human eye. Tao knelt down behind it, tapping a code into the suits rear hold. from it she pulled out a small capsule then tossed it onto the ground. As it hit the ground it let out a small hiss, expanding rapidly into a comfortable single air mattress. She laid down perching her head on the mattress's inbuilt, looked over at John with a faint smile that comforted him as he knelt down running his mechanical fingers through the coal.

“Well we made it this far, Considering the circumstances, I’ll take that as a plus”. John nodded in agreeance, reached behind his pack and pulled out a cylindrical device, scooping up some of the coal into it’s belly, Then tossed it to Tex. “Here, top this up” Tex diverted some of the water flow into the canister, heated the canister. pressure pushed the heated water in a vacuum pushing it through the charcoal producing clear clean water out the other side. Tex swirled the contents veering through the transparent half of the cylinder eyeing the water inside, took a swig, nodded in approval, “Earth water, Doesn’t get much better than that” and passed the cylinder back to John with curious eyes. John drank from it without hesitation. “I’m still collecting myself after Shai’s piloting display back there”. Shai chuckled humbly perched up against the cave wall as she reached over to take a drink from the canister. “Thanks Walker. you weren’t too bad yourself”.

Tex was still scouring the walls of the cave recouping the hydrogen reserves, he shut off his burner, walked over to John’s suit, knelt down and pulled out a large hydrogen cell, exchanging it for his own in his suit, re-fired his burner up and resumed scathing the walls for any ice. The whole motion of the cell exchange seemed like he was handling a foam cylinder. Despite the cell’s weight, the suit made little work handling the solid mass packed with platinum conversion cores “John, don’t you find it a little strange that we didn’t receive any notification from Commands long range transmitters of any enemy missiles headed our way, that and also, 68% may not be a solid signature on the plume. But, put two and two together, I think that bumps that % up to 100”, “We don’t know just yet big guy. best not to make any assumptions. with the severity of the blizzard, they could have simply lost connection to our receivers” Tao looked over at John with suspicious eyes, then looked over to Tex. “The captain's right, We can’t run on assumptions this soon”. Tex let out a snort in disproval “I don’t trust that fucker, he gives me chills”.

Shai walked over to Tex, laid her hand softly on his cladded shoulder like a blossom petal falling in a cold winter on polished granite “take a break buddy, I’ll get the other cells” watching his blood pressure lower in her HUD, she fired up her Ice burner and a slurping sound echoed off the walls once more, “Why does everything remind me of her” Tex smirked as he joked. John shook his head, “Well good to see you can still maintain a sense of humour even if the odds are stacked against us”, “I’m more concerned for his x if this reminds him of her, what did you do to the poor girl?” Shai turned around looking directly at Tex. “Well, they don’t call me Big guy for nothing” Tex sat down nearby the main entrance to the cave, letting out a sigh as he lowered himself to the ground in his suit “I heard your x used to refer to you as tiny?” John raised his eyebrows although the rest of his face was expressionless. “Yep! Big guy, Tiny heart”, Tex shrugged as he finished his sentence. “I think it’s the other way around with a touch of sarcasm on the first one” Shai was smiling inside her suit, but the others couldn’t see it, she knew the big guy was more sentimental than he let off. It’s also why she felt she could calm the mass of muscle when he got worked up.

“Alright well I don’t know about the rest of you but I could use some shut eye, whatever the Fuck is going on, it’ll make more sense on a clear mind” reached over pulling a small cylindrical device from his suit’s utility hold. He placed it on the cavern floor next to the now cold dormant fireplace, primed a timer to 5 seconds, and laid his heavy body comfortably a safe distance from the device as it chimed down to zero.Air  Particles ionized, then sintered in a brief display of dancing lights in the air around it from it emerged what felt like the soul of a jelly fish born from flame, its tentacles trails of smoke, gracing down to the cave floor. The room turned almost instantly warmer as the device beamed an amber glow in the cylinder’s vicinity.  John laid his head back, let out a deep sigh as he gazed at the cave ceiling. A blinking hydrogen cell light dimly lit the. “I know one thing, It’s nice to be out of zero G”, “And to be breathing non-filtered air” Tex said in agreeance as he popped off the modular housing from his sherpa rifle for a routine clean and inspection. “Wake you up in 20 cap, we should be restocked by then” said Shai. John closed his eyes, Tau laid still on her side looking over at John, slowly drifting off to the humming burn of Shai’s Ice burner. John fell into a deep sleep, his chest rising and falling slowly.

“You think that’s all John in there still” Tex spoke softly, not to disturb Siante and Walker. “Feels like it, but I know what you mean, he seems different.. quieter, I mean for all we know he’s still processing everything internally”, “He seems to be holding up alright, notice anything odd on his vitals”, “They’re more or less the same, I haven’t really had the time to run a proper analysis”, “Well you just give me the word if you need me to, you know”, “I don’t know Tex, I trust him, It’s not like he’s ever given us a reason not to”, “He stepped into an unknown piece of technology over a century old, he put the integrity of the squad at risk”, “I know, it doesn’t seem like John, but we have to trust him. If we lose John given all he’s done, well who can we really trust then”. Tex sat quietly for a moment digesting his thoughts. “And what if that LRM was Marcellus, what then? what are we supposed to, face the protectant on our own, Go into hiding? I wouldn’t mind being a nomad if you ask me. I could do it”. Shai stopped for a moment her burner went silent as the suit drained the last remaining fluid in it’s lines, an amber light on her suit’s hydrogen cell turned green indicating full capacity. “Honestly I don’t know right now Tex, but I know one thing, John will get us out of this. He always does”. She was even softer in her voice this time, more convincing. “Alright, If you say so tiger” Tex, seemed reserved in his response, but he let his shoulders down with a deep sigh. “I do know of an old friend in Nepal, nerdy type, he might be able to get his hands on a stealth frigate to get us out flying under the radar, I haven’t spoken to him in a decade, but I’m sure he’s still lurking around in the shadows somewhere, Nerdy but slippery that fucker”. Shai chuckled a little at Tex’s comment. “I think any option is a good option right now, big guy”, she agreed. Shai and Tex got lost for a few minutes, reminiscing stories of the lost war, their past missions together recalling all the times they’d got out “By a hair”.

Before Tau and John awoke soon enough Shai had recharged all 4 hydrogen Cell’s. “Do you think we should give them a couple more minutes?” Said Shai, looking into her HUD observing their sleep state and fatigue levels. “I know one thing, If that was Marcellus it’s only a matter of time before he gets a drone down here to finish the job, and I don’t particularly want to be waiting around when that happens, best we high tail it until we can glean more information”, “agreed, we need to keep moving, we don’t know what other secrets we might find down here, lets wake them up”. Shai tapped her HUD immediately after her statement. The neural implants on Tau and Shai tingled in the back of their necks waking them gently from their slumber. “All cells are recharged Cap” Shai smiled her gauntlet held out with an open palm to help Tau up. Tau grabbed onto the cold steel of Shai’s gauntlet, her skin slightly sticking as she let go. “those suit’s really take the affection out of a good gesture.. thanks”, “strange, I still feel every touch like it’s the suit isn’t even there, the Engineers really did a good job triangulating the nerve centers to the static shorting on the suit’s surface” Shai was trying to defend the suit, and kitten couldn’t agree more. “It took them almost 2 decades to get it right!” kitten chimed. “Alright enough chit chat. We need to keep moving” John was already climbing back into his suit. Tex looked over at Shai and shrugged his shoulders. “Fine by me cap” Said Tex pulling his rifle up into his shoulder and cocking it. “Keep on the lookout, we still don’t know if scavengers are active in the area, or who owned those missiles.” John clicked on his HUD opening up a holographic overview of the tunnel layout. “I managed to pull these maps from the facility archives, this tunnel will take us straight to the bottom of the valley, from there we can get up some hard comms to the facilities transmitter, and try and make contact with the Commander”, “Aaah cap!,” Tex wasn’t happy with John’s announcement. “68%, yeahh.. I know Tex, but what’s the worst he’s gonna do, yell profanities at us from orbit? he’s up there, we are down here. Besides there is a tower transmitter atop the facility mountain, we can use the multipathing off the mountain's faces to scramble our location if you are concerned”, Tau looked over at Tex, “Checks out”, She shrugged her shoulders. “Ok, but if I find out it was him, I dibs first blows”. “Ok big guy you can get intimate with him all you like when you see him next, lets move then”. John made his way over to the tunnel and started making his way down. Rocks and rubble rolled knocking echoes through the tunnel which seemed to be endless. “Watch your step” Shai whispered softly, John looked back at her pausing for a brief second holstered his sherpa rifle in it’s mount on his back then continued to descend down into the tunnels depths as he gripped both sides of the tunnels damp walls. The others all mounted their rifles following behind him.

 “Wouldn’t it have been easier to just use our suits jump thrusters and jump from the mountain pass to touch down on the valley bottom?” Said Tex, “And what burn through half our reserve again?” “Tau’s right Tex, we don’t want to get caught in out in the open with few cards up our sleeve”. Tex’s demeanour lacked effort, the big guy was getting bored with all the climbing. He preferred fast paced environments and detested the monotony of it all. “How much fucking longer is this going to take” he thought to himself. “Not far left, we are almost at the saddle we are at 17,500 feet … it plateaus out at approximately 17,000  feet.”, “Yikes wasn’t the old base camp for Everest around that?”, “probably why we are seeing scavenger activity in the area. the pass isn’t far from it it seems”. Shai was listening intently, “So much history in such a strange place of the world, We are lucky to experience it if you ask me”. “I guess you could say that”, Tau said in agreeance.

The strain on their legs eased as the tunnel began to level off. John grabbed his Sherpa rifle from it’s mount, reseating it against his shoulder. One by one the others following suit as they regained their balance behind him. “John, I’m detecting a heat signature up ahead” Shai was uncertain in her tone, “But, it doesn’t appear to be human, I’m detecting a 20% higher bpm”. John raised a closed fist, bringing the others to a halt. “Can we get a solid confirmation on that Shai?” said John, Kneeling to the floor.

Shai tapped on her wrist terminal gently. A small antenna array protruded then splayed out like small tendrons invisible to the human eye drifted in the breeze drawn down through the tunnel into the valley. They tendrons floated in the breeze listening, reverberating the distant heartbeat into life on Shai’s HUD, “Getting a closer analysis now Cap” Shai seemed more confident this time. “Aaah cap what’s showing up on the scan isn’t in our database, although it seems to be a large mammal, threat level low”. “I didn’t think any Mammals could survive in this region, or at least had been recorded here in over a century other than humans” Tau was surprised to hear. “Let’s keep moving, but stay alert” John steadily paced forward, one foot gently leading the other, his eyes rested vigilantly on his rifle site’s scanning each sector in a sweeping motion. The tunnel began to rapidly open out into a large cavernous maze. “Stick together” John was calm in his command, breathing gently as he paced steadily forward. “The opening is just up ahead”, “John, that heartbeat signature. It’s moving, not fast, but slowly, away from us” said Shai. John could see the opening up ahead of him. He turned off his HUD view for a moment then paused and retracted his helmet’s visor, the cold wind bit his face, but he thought nothing of it in the moment “I..”, John stopped still in his tracks, holding his breath as his gaze fixed dead ahead at the caves opening. Soft snow gently breezed through the mouth in the evening light. A lean grey figure seemed to slip like a shadow from the inner cavern’s wall into the opening. It stood there in still silence. It’s silhouette left John and the others in wonder, as the silhouettes eyes reflected an amber green back at them. They glared deep into John’s, still in time, two beings from different realms connected for a brief second. A bright light shone, the connection between John and the creature in an instant vanished as the figures eyes diverted to the beam emitted from Tex’s rifle torch. John raised his closed fist “Hold your…”  The figure stood still averting it’s gaze to Tex. A fraction of a second later it was gone. “What the fuck was that” Tex collected himself as he slowly lowered his weapon from where the creature once stood, he looked over at Shai waiting for an answer.

“Bringing it up now big guy”. The front half of an almost life-like three dimensional model, compiled from all four of their suit’s recorded images, materialized the creature from the pristine white surroundings of the valley’s backdrop. Its fur, a tapestry of muted grays and whites, seamlessly blended with the snowy canvas, had rendered the being almost invisible. its piercing eyes reflected what felt like ancient wisdom imbued with the prowess of survival. shades of greenish-gray, reminiscent of lichen-covered rocks from deep within the tunnel from where they’s once came, possessed an otherworldly brilliance. Intelligence exuded from the creature's keen eyes. “I didn’t think this possible Cap, but what we are seeing here, has long thought to be extinct. This explains why it didn’t show up on the database scan”, “Well, if it’s evolved over centuries of navigating this treacherous no-mans land, it’s no surprise it was thought to be extinct”. Tau looked at John, retracting her visor so he could see the joy in her face. “John.. that’s a snow leopard. They were hunted by scavengers in the region for their pelts, one pelt would feed a family for a year”. John paused reflecting on what had just happened. The gaze between him and his curious friend had been no casual encounter; but rare. An indelible mark had been left with him. In a silent ephemeral exchange of respect between one spirit in it’s home and the other, now lost.

“If she managed to remain hidden all this time with all the our scanning suite, what else could be hiding in these mountains”. At that John drew down his visor, stepping out into the thick blanket of snow crushing it helplessly beneath his boots. -10 Degrees Celsius fluctuated peaking at -12 on the teams HUD, but they couldn’t feel the colds bite, just the wind resistance as the storm pelted against their suits. “There is a clearing up ahead” Said John, determination stuck to his voice like cold steel. Tau stopped still in her“John, do.. do you see what I am
